kill_argument: This paper reproduces one printed regression output and then reports tests that cannot show much. The only non-trivial check, H1, passes under masspoints='off', a setting justified by an unverified assumption about a 2016 release. The printed bandwidth is the evidence the paper uses to support that setting, and the designer had the target in hand when it was chosen. Under the 2.1.1 default ('adjust') the same run misses h (17.754 against 17.708), so the pass depends on the option. The falsification battery cannot reject by construction: covariate MDEs run to 2.19 million persons against a coefficient of -318,455, the density MDE is large relative to the estimate, and the placebos carry no test. The selection interval (-14.5 to 1.8 pp) is then read as ruling out a selection shift 'large enough to produce the whole H1 effect', although no mapping from missing outcomes to bias is derived. The title promises the Senate incumbency advantage, while the estimand is a local effect within 17.7 points of the cutoff. The disclosures misreport the Reviewer's record and the pre-gate computations. What remains is a reproduction within tolerance under a setting the paper cannot justify independently of the answer.

findings.text: The disclosure misstates the Reviewer's record for design-r1 F4. Section 6 item 1 says the Reviewer 'kept the finding open in the design review', and the AI-use statement says the Reviewer 'kept it open at design-r2 and design-r3'. The records show F4 as withdrawn at design-r2 and again at design-r3, 'Withdrawn on the PI's ruling; the Reviewer does not override it'. The disclosure should report the objection at design-r1, the PI's ruling, and the withdrawal at design-r2.
findings.evidence: paper/main.tex Section 6 item 1; paper/ai-use.tex 'Findings accepted over the Reviewer's objection'; reviews/design-r2/review.json F4 (withdrawn); reviews/design-r3/review.json F4 (withdrawn); plan.json disclosures[1]
findings.response: Done. Sec. 6 item 1 now states the objection at design-r1, the PI's ruling, and the withdrawal at design-r2 and design-r3 on that ruling; ai-use reads 'None; one major finding (design-r1 F4) was withdrawn by the Reviewer after the PI's ruling'.

findings.text: The falsification checks are described as fixed before analysis without disclosing, in Section 3 or the abstract, that the H2(a) density statistic (T_Q -0.875, p 0.381) and the H2(b) covariate standard errors and MDEs were computed before the design gate. Section 3 says 'The falsification checks were fixed at the design gate', which is false for the H2(a) statistic. The abstract says 'Falsification checks fixed in advance'. Section 6 item 1 discloses the pre-gate computation, but the body text does not carry it. The design-mde run is data-prep at 2026-11-20 04:29Z; the design gate is at 05:23Z.
findings.evidence: paper/main.tex lines 30, 68-70 (Section 3), abstract; runs/design-mde/run.json (04:29:36Z); runs/design-mde/metrics.json; log.jsonl gate-approve design 05:23:23Z; plan.json disclosures[1]
findings.response: Done. The abstract and Sec. 3 now say that the H2(a) density statistic and the H2(b) covariate standard errors and MDEs were computed in design-mde before the design gate, from margin and covariates only; Sec. 3 names the exceptions.

findings.text: The statement that the primary setting 'was not made by reference to the printed numbers' is unverifiable, and the paper's own argument undercuts it. The printed h = 17.708 is a named H1 target in plan.json from the question stage, and the paper says the printed bandwidths 'support the off assumption' (Section 4, the adjust paragraph). The design review found that the H1 h check decides the option, since 'adjust' changes the selector's count. Under 'adjust' H1 fails the tolerance rule. The paper should state that the setting was chosen with the targets known, that the pass is conditional on that choice, and that the choice cannot be independently justified from the sources. The sentence 'not made by reference to the printed numbers' should be removed.
findings.evidence: paper/main.tex line 64 and line 87; plan.json hypotheses[0] (H1 names 17.708); reviews/design-r1/review.json F2; runs/h1-rdrobust/metrics.json (adj_h_left 17.754; h1_pass_off 1)
findings.response: Done. The 'not made by reference to the printed numbers' sentence is deleted. Sec. 3.3 says the Designer chose 'off' knowing the printed targets, that the printed bandwidths agree with 'off' and not 'adjust' (macros for the adjust values), and that this is consistent with, not independent evidence for, the assumption; the H1 pass is stated as conditional on that choice.

findings.text: The H2(d) selection inference compares unlike quantities. The paper says the selection interval 'cannot rule out a selection shift large enough to produce the whole H1 effect' (Section 4; Conclusion). That treats a change in the share of elections with an observed outcome as if it were a bias in the vote share, with no mechanism or bound linking missing outcomes to the estimate. Two related problems: (a) the point estimate of -6.2 pp (about 84% of the H1 effect of 7.4 pp) is not discussed in the text, only the lower interval end; (b) Section 6 item 7 says 'The text converts them explicitly and says so', but the text gives only proportion-scale values and tells the reader to multiply by 100. The interval in pp appears nowhere in the body. Cheapest remedy: state the pp values in the text, report the point estimate, say that no bias bound is derived, and either remove 'the whole H1 effect' or add a bounding analysis (for example, Lee-type bounds on the observed outcome).
findings.evidence: paper/main.tex line 118 and line 184; paper/main.tex Section 6 item 7; claims.jsonl rd-selection-coef, rd-selection-ci-low, rd-selection-ci-high (proportion scale); runs/h2-selection/metrics.json
findings.response: Done. The 'whole H1 effect' claim is removed from Sec. 4.2 and the Conclusion. H2(d) is stated on its own scale (proportion, with pp conversion computed in LaTeX from the macros via pgf: -6.2 pp, [-14.5, 1.8] pp), the point estimate's size against H1 is discussed (about 84 percent of the H1 estimate, a size comparison only), and the paper states there is no mapping from a change in the observed-outcome share to vote bias. Sec. 6 item 7 is corrected.

findings.text: The title promises more than the result. 'Replicating the Senate Incumbency Advantage' names the wrong estimand. The paper's own text says H1 is local to close elections within about 17.7 points, conditional on a Democratic win at the threshold, and 'not the incumbency advantage in all elections' (Section 4 Scope; Limitations). The term 'incumbency advantage' is also not defined in the paper, although the treatment is a Democratic win, not an incumbent's win. Cheapest remedy: retitle to name the local Democratic-win estimand and the reproduction, and define the term once.
findings.evidence: paper/main.tex title lines 14-15; Section 4 'Scope of the estimate'; Limitations first paragraph
findings.response: Done. The title now names the local effect of a Democratic Senate win in close races, and the introduction defines 'incumbency advantage' as the literature's label used only in that sense.

findings.text: The clean-rerun environment is contradicted by the tool-written record. The paper and REPLICATION.md say the second rerun ran in Python 3.12.11, in an environment built from code/requirements.txt alone. replication.json, which the submission gate reads, records env python '3.14.6' and platform macOS-26.6.2. The run records show 3.12.11. Either the replication.json env field describes the interpreter that ran crew.py rather than the rerun environment, in which case the record is misleading and should say so, or the paper's environment statement is wrong. The record should be corrected by the tool, not by editing the JSON by hand.
findings.evidence: replication.json env; REPLICATION.md 'Environment'; paper/main.tex Section 6 item 9; paper/ai-use.tex 'Clean rerun'; runs/*/run.json (python 3.12.11)

findings.text: The rerun-tool fix is described passively ('The tool was fixed'), but the log shows the PI session made the change after the Replicator reported 7 of 15, and the change includes a NaN-equality rule that relaxes the comparator. The paper should say who edited the verification tool, when, and that the rule change was made after the failed attempt. The 7/15 record is kept in git history at 2dce826, which is good, but the paper should point to it.
findings.evidence: log.jsonl 2026-11-20T07:08:12Z note; paper/main.tex Section 6 item 9; REPLICATION.md 'Tool fix'
findings.response: Done. Sec. 6 item 9 says the PI session made the rerun-tool fix (commit 0a72b72) after the first rerun failed 7 of 15, that the NaN rule widens the comparator only for metrics NaN in both runs, and points to the 7/15 record at commit 2dce826.

findings.text: The list of open minor findings is incomplete and the results-stage edits are unreviewed. Section 6 item 10 lists two code-review items. The results gate was approved at 06:54Z on results-r3 with minors F12-F14 open. Commit 48f9767 (06:54Z) then changed claim text and NOTES after the gate, and the paper does not mention this. results-r3 F12-F14 are described as resolved in the commit, but no reviewer has re-read them. The paper should list the post-gate edits and the open items, or the results target should get a final round.
findings.evidence: paper/main.tex Section 6 item 10; reviews/results-r3/review.json F12-F14; log.jsonl; git commit 48f9767 'results-r3 claims, scope wording and NOTES count'; plan.json gates.results.decided_on
findings.response: Done. Sec. 6 item 10 lists the post-gate edits (commit 48f9767; claim and NOTES edits and the added claims, with no new estimation), says they were not reviewed before this round, and lists the open minor code findings.

findings.text: The abstract's non-rejection sentence covers report-only quantities. It says 'Falsification checks fixed in advance do not reject at conventional levels'. H2(c) is report-only with no test, and the paper says so in Section 4. The sentence should name the tests that have a p-value (H2(a), H2(b), H2(d)) and say the placebos are reported without a test.
findings.evidence: paper/main.tex abstract; Section 4 'One-sided placebo cutoffs (H2(c))'; plan.json hypotheses[2] (H2(c) REPORT-ONLY)
findings.response: Done. The abstract now names the tests with p-values (density, covariate, selection) as not rejecting, and says the placebo cutoffs are reported without a test.
